explanations.examples: Fires on first-person statements of owning or having used a product/item, forum-review style: "I used to [[have]] one", "I have [[a]] stainless steel...". Peak lands on the possession verb or the token right after it (the article/object), once "I have/had/used (to have)" is established. Only two distinct top examples, so the breadth is inferred: I expect weaker firing for "I've used them", "Been using it", and third-person possession ("my wife has that"), and possibly French "j'ai". Should NOT fire on code, math, HTML, news prose, third-person narrative, finance text, or "have" as a pure auxiliary without an ownership/usage sense.
explanations.investigated: Fires on first-person owner/user testimony, forum style: "I used to have one", "I have a...", "I've been using/had them", "Mine/Ours are...". Not a past-tense detector: it peaks on the possession/usage verb, its object, or a possessive pronoun, and smears across the rest of the clause. Tiers: 0.75-0.87 of max ("Ours", "using" after I've been, "have one"); 0.4-0.6 ("I've had", "I have a", "Been running it" with dropped subject); 0.2-0.35 (French "j'ai acheté", "I owned" in cold context, obligation "I have to"). Strongly context-boosted by preceding first-person ownership sentences. Silent on third-person narrative, news, finance, code, maths, and mostly on third-person possession. Causal: ablation did essentially nothing (KL 0.0001).
